name: Duloxetine North American SUI
question: Does duloxetine reduce incontinence episodes and improve incontinence-related quality of life versus placebo in North American women with stress urinary incontinence?

design.population: 683 North American women aged 22–84 years with predominant stress urinary incontinence, at least seven stress episodes weekly, a positive cough stress test and stress pad test, and tolerance of retrograde bladder filling to 400 mL.
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1260

verdictNote: Both prespecified primary outcomes favored duloxetine; adverse-event withdrawal was higher.
takeaway: In 683 women with predominant stress incontinence, duloxetine 40 mg twice daily versus placebo reduced median weekly incontinence episodes by 50.0% versus 27.5% among women with a post-randomization diary and improved I-QOL scores over 12 weeks; adverse-event withdrawal was 24.1% versus 4.1%.

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation and Crossref publication metadata state October 2003 without a day
reports.citation: Dmochowski RR, Miklos JR, Norton PA, Zinner NR, Yalcin I, Bump RC. "Duloxetine versus placebo for the treatment of North American women with stress urinary incontinence." *J Urol.* 2003;170(4 Pt 1):1259-1263. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000080708.87092.cc
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1260

results.measure: Median percent decrease in weekly incontinence episode frequency, ITT with at least one post-randomization diary, 12 weeks
results.note: ITT included women with at least one post-randomization diary (83% of 344 duloxetine; 95% of 339 placebo); exact analysis counts and confidence interval were not reported. Last observation carried forward for early discontinuation.
results.locator: Full text, Table 1; Materials and Methods, p 1260

results.measure: Mean improvement in I-QOL total score, ITT with at least one post-randomization questionnaire, 12 weeks
results.note: ITT included women with at least one post-randomization I-QOL questionnaire (97% of 344 duloxetine; 98% of 339 placebo); exact analysis counts and confidence interval were not reported. Last observation carried forward for early discontinuation.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2; Results and Materials and Methods, p 1260

results.endpoint: At least 50% reduction in incontinence episodes
results.measure: Proportion with 50%–100% reduction in weekly incontinence episode frequency, ITT diary analysis
results.note: Exact responder counts and diary-analysis denominators were not reported.

results.measure: Mean increase in voiding interval, ITT analysis, 12 weeks
results.note: Exact analysis denominators and confidence interval were not reported.

results.measure: Median absolute decrease in weekly incontinence episodes, ITT diary analysis
results.note: Exact diary-analysis denominators and confidence interval were not reported.

results.endpoint: No incontinence episodes at last diary
results.measure: Proportion with no incontinence episodes at the last diary, ITT diary analysis
results.note: Exact event counts and diary-analysis denominators were not reported.

results.measure: Proportion rating condition improved on PGI-I during randomized treatment
results.note: Exact event counts and analysis denominators were not reported.

harms.label: Discontinuation because of adverse events
harms.note: P<0.001; 89% of adverse-event discontinuations occurred within the first four weeks. Exact event counts were not reported.

harms.label: Nausea-associated discontinuation and completion

values.exp: 22.7% of 344 randomized women (78 women) had nausea; 6.4% discontinued because of nausea; 58/78 (74%) with nausea completed
values.ctl: 2.1% of 339 randomized women had nausea; none discontinued because of nausea

harms.note: Treatment-emergent nausea was the most common adverse event; P<0.001 for incidence and nausea-associated discontinuation.

harms.label: Other treatment-emergent adverse events

values.exp: 74% had any event; fatigue 14.8%, insomnia 14.2%, dry mouth 12.2% of 344 randomized women
values.ctl: 50% had any event; fatigue 3.8%, insomnia 2.4%, dry mouth 0.9% of 339 randomized women

harms.note: Any-event comparison P<0.001; each listed event P<0.001.

delivery.label: Study regimen
delivery.value: A two-week no-drug lead-in and two-week blinded placebo lead-in preceded randomization to duloxetine 40 mg twice daily or matching placebo for 12 weeks, with visits every four weeks.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1260

delivery.label: Treatment completion and adherence

values.exp: 69% of 344 randomized women completed 12 weeks; mean 80% of doses ingested
values.ctl: 87% of 339 randomized women completed 12 weeks; mean 93% of doses ingested

delivery.note: P<0.001 for both completion and dose ingestion; lower duloxetine adherence was driven by early discontinuation.
